newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds grind to a halt ahead of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds grind to a halt ahead of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Eurobond primary market activity was almost at a standstill Friday as the wider financial community awaited U.S. jobs data for July.
Next week's new issue calendar was pretty thin and syndicate managers were poised for the first summer lull in the Eurobond market for several years.
Among extremely limited new issue business this morning, LW Rentenbank set a 10 billion peseta three-year transaction with a 5.00 percent coupon via Banco Bilbao Vizcaya and Merrill Lynch.
Fannie Mae priced its hugely successful 10-year Australian dollar deal, giving the A$1.0 billion bond a 6.375 percent coupon and 99.635 issue/reoffer price.
Paper was bid at a yield spread of nine basis points on broker screens shortly after being freed to trade, from the 10 b.p. reoffer level.

The July U.S. employment report and June personal income and consumption figures were due at 1230 GMT, followed at 1400 GMT by the July National Association of Purchasing Management report and the final July University of Michigan sentiment index.
A Reuters survey of economists found an average forecast of a 193,000 rise in the non-farm payroll, after June's 217,000 gain.
